h1: Arcade Machine for Bar ROI: A Realistic Payback Timeline

outline.heading: Why Arcade Machine ROI Questions Deserve a Clear-Eyed Answer
outline.purpose: Frame the reader's real question, explain why most online answers (forum guesswork or vendor sales copy) are too vague to trust, and set up the article's numbers-first approach.

outline.heading: What Actually Drives Arcade Machine Profitability
outline.purpose: Explain the underlying variables that determine whether a machine performs well or poorly in a bar or venue setting, before presenting any numbers.

outline.heading: Foot Traffic and Venue Type
outline.purpose: Explain how venue type and customer volume influence realistic usage rates.

outline.heading: Revenue Split Between Bar and Machine Owner
outline.purpose: Clarify how revenue-sharing arrangements typically affect net income for the machine owner.

outline.heading: Seasonality and Slow Periods
outline.purpose: Address how off-season or slow-venue periods reduce weekly revenue and why this must be modeled honestly.

outline.heading: Maintenance and Electricity Costs
outline.purpose: Cover the recurring costs of running a machine so the reader understands gross revenue is not net profit.

outline.heading: Three Payback Scenarios: Pessimistic, Base Case, and Optimistic
outline.purpose: Introduce the scenario-modeling method and explicitly state the assumptions behind each labeled scenario.

outline.heading: Pessimistic Scenario Assumptions
outline.purpose: State low-traffic, low-revenue assumptions clearly as illustrative modeling inputs.

outline.heading: Base Case Scenario Assumptions
outline.purpose: State moderate, most-likely assumptions clearly as illustrative modeling inputs.

outline.heading: Optimistic Scenario Assumptions
outline.purpose: State high-traffic, high-revenue assumptions clearly as illustrative modeling inputs.

outline.heading: Comparison Table: Weekly Revenue and Payback Period by Scenario
outline.purpose: Present a single scannable table showing weekly revenue, key assumptions, and payback period in months for all three scenarios so the reader can verify the math at a glance.

outline.heading: Which Scenario Should You Actually Plan Around?
outline.purpose: Explain the relative probability of each scenario and make clear that the base case, not the optimistic case, is what a prudent operator should use for planning.

outline.heading: Net Monthly Profit After Payback: What Happens Next
outline.purpose: Show ongoing net monthly profit by scenario after the payback period, with named recurring costs subtracted, keeping every figure internally consistent with the earlier weekly numbers.

outline.heading: How This Model Was Built: Using a Real List Price to Run Your Own Numbers
outline.purpose: Explain the methodology, anchor the model to a real, checkable list price, and show readers how to substitute their own venue numbers.

outline.heading: Where the JVL ECHO Fits Into This Picture
outline.purpose: A single, soft-touch section near the end connecting the analysis to the JVL ECHO product page, clearly distinguishing the Commercial Edition (venue use) from the Home Edition (home leisure use), and linking naturally to jvl.ca/en/echo.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.purpose: Placeholder for the FAQ Agent to populate with at least 5 FAQ blocks addressing objections such as revenue per week, good ROI benchmarks, payback timing, revenue splits, maintenance, and electricity costs.

outline.heading: Assumptions and Limitations
outline.purpose: Disclose plainly that all revenue figures, splits, and cost estimates are illustrative modeling assumptions for reader-verifiable math, not sourced industry statistics.
